name: Serpentine-Dusk
description: Serpentine-Dusk is a warm desert world whose terrain undulates in sinuous curves of green-veined rock, the serpentine mineral that gives the planet its name. Rolling dune seas of olive and jade-colored sand stretch between mountain ranges of dark, polished stone, and the dry beds of ancient rivers carve winding paths across the landscape like the tracks of enormous snakes. The planet's slow rotation creates extended twilights that last for hours, bathing the serpentine terrain in amber light.

The breathable atmosphere is dry but rich in oxygen, produced by vast colonies of photosynthetic organisms that live within the sand itself, coloring the dunes their characteristic green. Fauna adapted to the desert heat emerges at dusk, filling the cooling air with chitinous rustling and low, resonant calls. The scent of sun-baked mineral dust mingles with something organic and alive, a reminder that this desert breathes.

Scattered across the planet at irregular intervals stand monolithic structures of smooth black stone, each precisely three meters tall, each oriented toward a different star. No two face the same direction, and their arrangement suggests a catalog or map of stellar positions from an epoch thousands of years past. The local fauna treats the monoliths as territorial markers, circling them but never touching.

Serpentine-Dusk's combination of breathable air and abundant solar energy makes it a viable colony site despite the heat, and the thriving desert ecosystem demonstrates long-term climate stability. The monoliths resist all attempts at dating or material analysis, their composition unlike any known substance. Colonization advocates argue the monoliths are ancient and irrelevant; others suggest that anything so precisely placed may still serve a purpose that has not yet become apparent.
